t:
That title 14 of the
United States Code, entitled “Coast Guard”, is hereby revised, codified, and enacted into law, and may be cited as “Title 14, United States Code, section —”, as follows:

fable.w: This is only an enacting clause that codifies Title 14 (Coast Guard) into positive law and gives its citation form. It names no outside party, and provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. One might guess that the codified title contains participatory provisions somewhere, but none appear in this section's text.
fable.s: is hereby revised, codified, and enacted into law

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard enacting clause for a codification or revision of a title of the United States Code. It does not contain any substantive provisions regarding consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely establishes the legal citation and enactment of the revised title.
qwen_block.s: That title 14 of the United States Code, entitled “Coast Guard”, is hereby revised, codified, and enacted into law, and may be cited as “Title 14, United States Code, section —”, as follows:

opus.w: This section only says that title 14 of the U.S. Code is revised, codified and enacted into law. It mentions no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, right to sue, or any other way for people outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. Nothing in it touches on participation, so the quoted span is empty.
opus.b: There is no tempting reading here. This is only an enacting clause that codifies title 14 ("Coast Guard"). It describes no federal decision process and no outside party.

qwen_chat.w: The section is a purely legislative housekeeping provision that revises, codifies, and cites Title 14 of the U.S. Code. It does not establish any advisory bodies, public comment periods, consultations with non-federal entities, or rights to sue. There are no outside parties involved in any decision-making process described in this text.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section establishes a new title of the U.S. Code, it implicitly creates a framework for future participation. However, the text provided is merely a codification and citation instruction. It does not describe any specific process, committee, hearing, or consultation mechanism. It contains no actors outside the federal government and no procedural requirements for decision-making. Therefore, it fails the definition of participation.
